question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

A student may not withdraw after the published deadline [15]. For extraordinary circumstances that prevented a timely withdrawal, the Office of the Provost accepts late administrative withdrawal appeals. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the extraordinary circumstances, why standard procedures could not be followed (or incompletes were not obtained), and the term. Typically, an approved appeal results in W grades for all courses in that term; exceptions may be considered in extraordinary circumstances [16].

Withdrawing from a course may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress toward graduation [11]. Financial Aid says federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits after the refund period; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed. It recommends discussing your aid with Financial Aid before withdrawing [41]. SAP is reviewed annually after spring; students must complete at least 67% of credits attempted, and undergraduate/graduate students must meet cumulative GPAs of 2.0/3.0, respectively [2]. The college pages don't establish the effect on your individual aid or SAP status; contact Financial Aid to discuss your situation [1][41].

Its published details do not establish the effect on your particular aid for one class withdrawn after the deadline. For SAP, aid eligibility is reviewed annually after spring; students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits and meet the GPA standard (undergraduates 2.0; graduates 3.0) [2]. The pages don’t determine your individual aid or SAP outcome.

Financial Aid recommends discussing your current aid with its office [1].
